Team / GCP,

Thanks for joining the kickoff thread — we're aiming to finalize the commercial enablement and the orderflow (billing + purchase path) for the Acme GCP listing by the end of November. Goals for the thread:

- Capture the canonical orderflow (purchase path via GCP, invoice model, subscription vs. metered).
- Surface any gaps in procurement/customer POs, DocuSign routing, and GCP billing mapping.
- Agree on operational touchpoints (who owns entitlements, refunds, invoices).

Initial asks:
1) Jordan: can you map current Redwood billing models to the GCP SKU model and call out any transformation logic we need?
2) Vanessa: please surface Acme's procurement constraints (payment terms, PO process) — Samir, can you ask your procurement team to confirm?
3) Karthik: scope any console/metadata fields we need to expose for co-sell reporting.

I've attached a rough draft of the orderflow (orderflow-draft.pdf) — mainly a strawman to annotate. Please reply with top-line comments by EOD Monday (16 Nov).

Subject: Re: Design: Commercial enablement & orderflow for GCP Marketplace listing

Naomi — quick pass from billing perspective. Thanks for the draft.

Notes:
- Redwood models: we support per-token metered and subscription (seat/commit) today. GCP SKUs will want flat monthly SKUs + usage-based SKUs. We'll need a reconciliation layer that emits both a GCP SKU usage file and our internal usage records.
- Tax & invoicing: if Acme requires direct invoicing, we need to confirm whether the purchase will be handled through GCP (reseller flow) or via a direct contract + billing transfer. Both have different refund paths.
- Edge case: cancellations mid-cycle — do we pro-rate on GCP or on Redwood ledger? Recommend pro-rate on Redwood and submit a monthly adjustment to GCP (simpler).

Action items from me: I'll draft a mapping doc and a sample invoice flow by Monday (16 Nov).

Following up with Acme-specific constraints. Samir — thanks for the intro earlier this week. A couple of things we learned from Acme procurement (see attached MAUP worksheet):

- Acme requires PO numbers for any order > $10k and standard 60-day payment terms.
- They want a single consolidated monthly invoice with line items broken down by SKU and usage buckets.
- They prefer DocuSign routing to their central procurement inbox (procurement@acme.com).
